text:
support-engineer: Customer FinLink (tenant t-finlink-42) reports repeated 5xx and timeouts since 10:12 UTC. Multiple error batches, p95 up and p99 huge. Posting sample request_id and logs we got from their support payload.

ingest-bot: alert: hosted.gateway.queue_depth > 1500 for pool hosted-prod-eu-west1 (sustained 10m). continuous_batcher.backlog=1320. p95_response_time=2.4s p99=12.1s.

yara: @kai can you pull the gateway traces for those request_ids? suspect continuous-batching backlog + kvcache churn. any recent kernel/runtime changes deployed?

kai: pulling traces now. no runtime kernel change in last 6h. I see a pattern: lots of long sequences hitting the continuous batcher, many small requests queuing behind a few long tokens. sample ids: rq_9f8e7d2a, rq_a1b2c3d4, rq_7e6f5a1b.

support-engineer: repro curl we got from customer: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gptx-13b","input":"summarize...","max_tokens":1500}'` -> immediate 502/504 or `Upstream read timeout` after ~30s.

yara: metrics snapshot from the same window: `continuous_batcher.backlog=1320, queue_depth=1765, inflight_longseq=48, kvcache_hit_rate=0.62, batch_fill_pct=87%`. That batch_fill_pct + backlog implies long queues forming behind heavy longseq customers.

kai: I pulled a trace for rq_9f8e7d2a: enqueued at gateway -> queued 6.4s -> batched -> worker started after 11.9s -> token generation stalls due to kvcache eviction thrash -> worker timed out on deadline -> gateway 504 bubbled up.

sre-oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) toggle tenant continuous batching off (`tenants.t-finlink-42.continuous_batching=false`) 2) bump pool scale by +2 GPUs in eu-west for 15m 3) apply per-tenant max_seq or rate-limit (eg. max_seq=512) 4) route FinLink to a fallback smaller model variant to reduce token costs. Which do we want now?

support-engineer: Customer is on-prod and time-sensitive. Requesting fastest fix: toggle continuous batching off for tenant + short autoscale bump. They can tolerate slightly higher token costs for now.

yara: I can disable continuous batching for t-finlink-42 now. Doing `PATCH /controlplane/tenants/t-finlink-42` payload: `{"continuous_batching": false}`. Will monitor backlog.

ingest-bot: audit: PATCH tenant t-finlink-42 continuous_batching=false by yara at 10:25:40 UTC.

kai: scaled hosted-prod-eu-west1 pool +2 gpus (hot-add). Confirmed new workers registered; batcher backlog started to drop but still slow. queue_depth -> 980 after scale up.

support-engineer: updated customer: "We disabled continuous batching for your tenant and added temporary capacity — you should see errors drop. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with permanent mitigations." They replied :thumbsup: and provided another failing request_id (rq_b2c3d4e5) showing 502 earlier this morning too.

yara: post-mitigation metrics (10:35 UTC): continuous_batcher.backlog=180, queue_depth=420, p95=0.42s, p99=1.6s. Improvement visible.

kai: root cause notes for postmortem: bursty long-sequence traffic from FinLink + continuous batching heuristics filling batches with longseq -> kv-cache churn and eviction thrash -> worker slowdown -> queue buildup and tail timeouts. Mitigations: per-tenant max_seq guardrail, adaptive batching thresholding (cap batch fill for tenants with >N longseq), and better kvcache sizing.

sre-oncall: action items: `- yara: revert continuous_batching=false once we have safe rollout for adaptive batching (or keep off and schedule rollback) - kai: follow up with a kvcache sizing runbook and simulate longseq churn - support-engineer: coordinate customer follow-up and capture exact repro payloads for longseq flows`

support-engineer: thanks all. I'll log a customer incident update and request their sample payloads + traffic pattern. Will reopen if errors recur.

ingest-bot: incident-note: FinLink outage mitigation at 10:25 UTC: toggled continuous batching and scaled pool. Backlog cleared.

yara: saving traces and creating incident doc draft in #postmortems. I'll link the trace ids and the metrics graphs.

support-engineer: closing thread for now, will update with postmortem link.
